question: to the Commission Pina Picierno (S&D) Subject:

Launched in 1996, ‘Your Europe Advice’ is a Commission-funded service that provides free and tailored legal advice to citizens and businesses regarding their internal market and EU citizenship rights. On average, the service handles over 30 000 queries every year, responding by email or phone in any of the 24 official EU languages within a week. Your Europe Advice (YEA) also assists national SOLVIT centres, which provide Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) services. News recently broke that the European Commission’s Directorate General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs has decided that it will not issue a call for tenders for YEA, which will no longer be available as of 1 September 2026. In the light of the above: 1.

Could the Commission clarify why it is discontinuing a popular service that provides direct and tailored assistance to citizens and businesses and why this decision was taken without a public consultation?
Has an assessment been carried out to assess the impact this decision will have on citizens, SOLVIT centres and other DGs?
Was consideration given to the possibility of transferring the management of this service to another DG?
